iterations.strategy: Category A (plan restructuring / work elimination). Diagnosis: the dominant phase (name_filter, 12ms of 68ms) ran an expensive memmem LIKE on all 4.17M name rows even though only ~14% have a matching aka_name row and could possibly contribute to the final join. The previous order built name_bits first and then derived aka_bits as a subset — doing the costly work on rows that were doomed to fail the aka_name semi-join anyway. New order: (1) scan aka_name/person_id.bin into aka_has bitset (~3.6MB sequential, ~1-2ms), (2) name filter gated as aka_has[id] && gender==code && LIKE — short-circuit ordering puts the cheapest tests first so memmem only runs for the rare survivor. The two bitsets collapse into one (name_bits encodes name predicate AND has-aka), so the inner ci loop does a single bitset probe instead of two. All other physical choices (primary-CSR range scans into the three fact tables, dense-id arithmetic for char_name existence and name-row recovery, thread-local MIN reduction) are preserved from iter_0 — they were not the bottleneck.
